questions.question: Why should cargo tanks never be completely full?

options.text: Liquid expands as it gets warmer.
Regulations require three feet of space between the liquid and the tank roof.
A full tank would be too heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Liquid expands as it gets warmer.
questions.explanation: Liquids expand when heated. You must leave extra space in the tank for this expansion. Different liquids expand different amounts, so know the requirements for your specific cargo.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, how does stopping distance change?

options.text: It is longer than on normal roads.
It is shorter than on normal roads.
It is about the same as on normal roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is longer than on normal roads.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on slippery surfaces because your tires have less grip on the road.

questions.question: If your cargo is leaking, what should you do?

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify it.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.
Assume all cargo is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.
questions.explanation: If hazardous cargo leaks, identify it using shipping papers, labels, or package location. Never touch the leaking material.

questions.question: Which behavior shows aggressive driving?

options.text: Planning extra time for your trip.
Slowing down and keeping safe distance from other vehicles.
Making hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making hand gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by allowing extra travel time, keeping safe distance from others, and never making gestures that anger other drivers.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Pull into a service station.
Call emergency services and tell them your location.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull into a service station.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Report the fire and your location to emergency services.

questions.question: While driving, if you hear an unusual noise or feel something wrong, you should:

options.text: Ignore it and keep driving.
Hope the vehicle works until the next driver takes over.
Stop and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: Pay attention to what you see, hear, smell, and feel while driving. If anything seems wrong, stop and investigate to find the problem.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.
Remove the relay valves.
Close the emergency line valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the emergency line valve.
questions.explanation: Before your trip, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all brake systems on all trailers. Listen for escaping air. Then close both shut-off valves before you drive.

questions.question: When ice starts to melt as temperature rises, what happens?

options.text: It is usually safe to drive.
The road becomes even more slippery.
Traction improves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes even more slippery.
questions.explanation: As ice melts, water sits on top of the ice, making the road even slippier. Drive slowly and carefully on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What should you do with wheel rims that have been welded?

options.text: Paint them.
Put them on tires at the back of the vehicle.
Do not use them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use them.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe and should not be used.

questions.question: In bad weather, what do many car drivers do around trucks?

options.text: Drive in front of trucks.
Drive to the sides of trucks.
Follow trucks too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow trucks too closely.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, many car drivers follow large trucks too closely, especially when visibility is poor.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
Prevents a truck from being stolen
Prevents the driver from driving too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically if the pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Is texting while operating a CMV legal?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
Yes, it is acceptable on rural roads.
Yes, it is acceptable when contacting your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous. It is illegal to text while operating a CMV.

questions.question: How can you best tell if your trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: By watching other drivers' faces
By checking the trailer in your mirrors
By feeling the trailer move

questions.correctAnswerText: By checking the trailer in your mirrors
questions.explanation: The best way to notice that your trailer has started to skid is to watch it in your mirrors. This lets you spot the problem as early as possible.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle
Push the clutch out when the engine is close to idle
Shift into neutral when the engine is close to idle

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle
questions.explanation: When stopping, apply steady pressure to the brake pedal and stop smoothly. In a manual transmission vehicle, push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Makes your stopping distance shorter
Does not change how you apply the brakes
Allows you to drive faster

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change how you apply the brakes
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps prevent brakes from locking up during hard braking. You should brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without it. It does not necessarily make your stopping distance shorter.

questions.question: When is hydroplaning most likely to happen?

options.text: When traveling faster than 60 mph
When tire pressure is too low
When tire tread is too deep

questions.correctAnswerText: When tire pressure is too low
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely to happen on wet roads when tire pressure is too low and tire tread is too worn. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a curve?

options.text: Shift into neutral
Use the shoulder
Downshift

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift
questions.explanation: Always slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Never the same way two times in a row
Always in the same order
They do not need to be done if you know the vehicle well

questions.correctAnswerText: Always in the same order
questions.explanation: Complete a vehicle inspection in the same order every time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes it less likely that you will forget to check something.

questions.question: How should you apply brakes in a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The same way as you would in a vehicle without ABS
As the vehicle is placed in neutral
Using only the hand brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way as you would in a vehicle without ABS
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with ABS, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What does a driver need to accept a hazardous materials package?

options.text: The shipper's certification
A notarized statement
A verbal agreement

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper's certification
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that the package is prepared correctly. Unless a package is clearly unsafe or does not follow Hazardous Materials Regulations, you can accept the shipper's certification that the package is properly prepared.
